subject: Clarify BAA scope for proxying and on-prem de-identification
messages:
From: Dana Morris <dana.morris@medicorehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Clarke <evan.clarke@hc-privacy-consult.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify BAA scope: upstream proxy + de-id before storage

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're trying to map how MediCore would route inbound patient records (PDF intake forms + short voice notes) into Redwood for downstream classification and summary. Two specific questions to confirm before our security team will accept a BAA: 

1) If we send data through a customer-managed proxy that performs deterministic de-identification (PII removal) before any tokens hit Redwood-hosted endpoints, does Redwood consider that traffic "PHI in scope" for the BAA, or does the BAA scope exclude data that has already been de-identified in transit?

2) For scenarios where MediCore wants Redwood to run an on-prem de-id step (we'd host a lightweight de-id container in our VPC that calls your model), do you require a Dedicated/Private deployment for that, or will Hosted with specific contract language suffice (we're OK paying an add-on)?

We're also attaching a diagram of the proposed ingest path. Evan is our privacy consultant and will help with technical details.

Appreciate a short clarification — the security reviewers are meeting Thursday.

Best,
Dana

--
Dana Morris
Head of Product Security, MediCore Health
Dana.Morris@medicorehealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Dana Morris <dana.morris@medicorehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Evan Clarke <evan.clarke@hc-privacy-consult.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify BAA scope: upstream proxy + de-id before storage

Hi Dana — thanks for the clear diagram and the questions. Short answers up front:

- If the data has been de-identified (per HIPAA expert guidance) before it reaches any Redwood-hosted processing or storage, that data is generally considered out of scope for a BAA. However, we need to agree on the de-id method and evidence that the de-id is irreversible.
- For an on-prem de-id container that calls Redwood models: if the PHI never reaches our hosted runtime (i.e., you run de-id locally and only non-PHI tokens go to our API), Hosted plus contractual language can be acceptable. If your workflow requires raw PHI to be processed by Redwood-hosted models (even transiently), you will need Redwood Private or Dedicated with BAA coverage.

To make this actionable for your security team, I'd like to confirm three artifacts we usually need:
1) A brief de-identification spec (what fields/PII are removed and what algorithm is used).
2) A dataflow diagram showing exactly where tokens are transformed and which systems see raw data.
3) A signed BAA template; we can mark sections for dedicated vs. hosted options.

I'm looping Marcus (infra/architecture) who can review the diagram Evan provided and confirm the deploy options and any technical caveats around our streaming endpoints. I'll follow up with a redline-friendly BAA draft.

Best,
Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Dana Morris <dana.morris@medicorehealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Clarke <evan.clarke@hc-privacy-consult.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify BAA scope: upstream proxy + de-id before storage

Hi Dana — Marcus here. Quick technical clarifications after looking at your diagram (attached flow renamed to ingest-proxy-deid-flow.png):

- If your proxy deterministically removes direct identifiers (name, SSN, MRN, exact DOB) and replaces them with one-way hashes, and if the hashed values are never reversible by MediCore, Redwood would treat that as de-identified for BAA scoping.
- Be cautious with quasi-identifiers (free-text notes, rare-condition mentions) — de-id needs to address re-identification risk. Our privacy team will ask for sample inputs/outputs (redacted) to validate.
- For audio notes: performing on-prem voice-to-text + PII redaction before any outbound call ensures PHI never reaches our hosted runtime. If you plan to use our Hosted speech-to-text, that's within BAA scope.

I'll slot time Thursday 10am PT to walk through the diagram and the specific fields.

Thanks,
Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Principal Product Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Evan Clarke <evan.clarke@hc-privacy-consult.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dana Morris <dana.morris@medicorehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2026 07:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify BAA scope: upstream proxy + de-id before storage

On Thu, 6 May 2026 at 10:25, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> - For audio notes: performing on-prem voice-to-text + PII redaction before any outbound call ensures PHI never reaches our hosted runtime. If you plan to use our Hosted speech-to-text, that's within BAA scope.

Thanks for the clarification — a couple follow-ups from our side:

1) Can you confirm whether hashed identifiers (one-way) are acceptable when combined with "contextual metadata" (e.g., encounter date, facility code) which could enable re-identification? We typically recommend truncating or generalizing dates in addition to hashing.
2) If MediCore wants Redwood to perform only model inference on de-identified tokens but keep an audit trail linking original IDs locally (not sent to Redwood), can we add a clause in the BAA that the audit linkage remains 100% under MediCore control and Redwood will not request or retain any local ID mapping?

I'm compiling a short list of contractual language options to present to their legal team — would appreciate any sample clauses you can share.

Best,
Evan

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Dana Morris <dana.morris@medicorehealth.com>, Evan Clarke <evan.clarke@hc-privacy-consult.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 May 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify BAA scope: upstream proxy + de-id before storage

Hi Dana & Evan,

Thanks — this is helpful. Summary and next steps: 

- We consider upstream deterministic de-id (irreversible hashing + redaction of quasi-identifiers) out of BAA scope, provided you share the de-id specification and sample redacted outputs for our privacy review. We'll need to include explicit de-id acceptance criteria in the BAA.
- For audio: if you perform on-prem STT + redaction, Hosted is fine; otherwise audio STT via Redwood falls under BAA.
- Contractually: we're happy to add a clause stating Redwood will not request, store, or retain any external mapping that links de-identified tokens to original identifiers. We'll provide sample wording in the BAA redline (attached: redwood_baa-draft-v2.pdf).

Action items: 
1) Dana/Evan: send a brief de-id spec (1 page) and two sample redacted records by EOD Wednesday so our privacy team can validate.
2) Kimberly/Marcus: we'll send a redline of the BAA with de-id acceptance language and an optional Dedicated deployment appendix by Friday.

If that timeline works, I'll open the internal BAA ticket and loop legal. Thanks again — feel free to call if you want to walk through the spec live.

Best,
Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
